startState.researchCursor: precompressed single-file artifact transport, evidence transport, integrity/provenance, compression, artifact indexing

verifiedImprovement.summary: Ferrum desktop CI artifacts are now producer-owned tar.gz files uploaded directly with actions/upload-artifact archive:false, preserving executable permissions and making the provider artifact digest equal the locally verified archive SHA-256.
verifiedImprovement.rootCause: The prior Actions directory-artifact path preserved file contents but the zip round trip normalized file permissions. On Linux the downloaded Ferrum executable lost its execute bit, so a byte-identical downloaded package failed to launch with EACCES.

failureFirst.linuxObservation: The baseline downloaded directory artifact matched the original file-by-file SHA-256 manifest, but the real packaged Ferrum smoke failed at process launch with EACCES because dist/Ferrum-linux-x64/Ferrum was not executable.
failureFirst.significance: Content digest equality alone was insufficient to prove a runnable desktop deliverable. The artifact transport needed to preserve filesystem mode metadata as well as bytes.

isolatedExperiment.performanceConclusion: The archive:false raw upload stage was substantially faster, but tar creation and explicit extraction made the full producer-plus-consumer path slower in this comparison. The change is adopted for correctness, portability and integrity, not claimed as an end-to-end speedup.

behavior: Create a gzip level-1 tar archive from the complete packaged dist tree.
Record the original file-by-file SHA-256 manifest before archiving.
Delete dist, extract the produced archive into a fresh dist, recompute the manifest and require exact equality.
Run the existing real packaged Ferrum smoke against the freshly extracted archive on Linux and Windows.
Upload the exact verified tar.gz as one raw Actions artifact with archive:false.
Require actions/upload-artifact artifact-digest to exactly equal the locally calculated archive SHA-256.

ecosystemRotation: artifact transport, producer-owned archives, download integrity, provenance, compression, result/evidence interoperability

independentChallenge.question: What additional current technique would materially improve Ferrum artifact trust or agent usability without adding speculative complexity?
independentChallenge.strongestCandidate: actions/attest v4 signed provenance for the exact verified tar.gz
independentChallenge.reasonDeferred: The current run closed a demonstrated runnable-artifact defect and strengthened byte identity. Signed provenance is promising but adds permissions and a separate verifier path; it has not yet completed an identical-artifact Ferrum experiment proving enough incremental value to ship in the same run.

antiRegression.notes: All existing evidence uploads remain. The full Linux/Windows browser and desktop workflows still execute before artifact publication, and the portable archive adds an extra round-trip manifest and fresh-extraction runtime proof.

nextResearchCursor: Run a same-artifact actions/attest v4 provenance experiment and independently verify the exact downloaded Linux and Windows tar.gz artifacts with gh attestation verify.
Prototype a compact artifact-ID/digest/source/runtime evidence index and measure agent tool-call and payload reduction while retaining complete raw evidence.
Revisit dependency caching only after Ferrum has trustworthy reproducible dependency identity and explicit invalidation keys.
Resume process/sandbox isolation experiments after artifact transport and provenance work converges.

publication.verificationContract: Re-read the GitHub checkpoint after creation, append the same canonical checkpoint plus GitHub identity into the existing Drive recovery document, then re-read and export the Drive document for independent size/hash verification.
